# Markdown Writing Style

## Semantic Line Breaks

Apply [Semantic Line Breaks (SemBr)](https://sembr.org) to all prose.
Line breaks must not alter the final rendered output.

Break after every sentence,
as punctuated by a period (`.`), exclamation mark (`!`), or question mark (`?`).

Break after independent clauses
as punctuated by a comma (`,`), semicolon (`;`), colon (`:`), or em dash (`—`).

Break may occur after a dependent clause
to clarify grammatical structure or satisfy line length constraints.

Break before enumerated and itemized lists.

Do not break inside a hyphenated word.

## Line Length

Target 80 characters maximum per line.
Lines may exceed 80 characters to accommodate hyperlinks, code spans, or other markup.

## Lists

Add a semantic line break before every list.
Group related items without blank lines between them.
Use a blank line to separate logically distinct groups within a list.

## Code Blocks

Do not apply semantic line breaks inside fenced code blocks or inline code spans.
Code must be reproduced exactly as it would run.
